findings.why: A declare-then-build contract is only a ruling if every declared section exists in the artifact.

findings.title: Purple, violet or indigo gradient

evidence.snippet: background: linear-gradient(135deg, #eef2ff 0%, var(--bg) 45%, #fdf2f8 100%) | stop #eef2ff

findings.fix: Replace the purple stop with a neutral surface or the single declared accent.
findings.why: The named number one AI design tell: a saturated purple wash over a section.

findings.title: Color literal outside the token block

evidence.snippet: background: linear-gradient(135deg, #eef2ff 0%, var(--bg) 45%, #fdf2f8 100%) | literals: #eef2ff, #fdf2f8

findings.fix: Declare these as custom properties in the token block and reference them with var().
findings.why: A raw hex or rgb value in a component bypasses the token system, so the palette drifts one patch at a time.

findings.title: Artifact violates a ban from the contract

evidence.snippet: banned tell "purple-gradient" detected: background: linear-gradient(135deg, #eef2ff 0%, var(--bg) 45%, #fdf2f8 100%) | stop #eef2ff

findings.fix: Remove the banned tell, or remove it from contract.bans with a written reason.
findings.why: The contract listed this tell as banned: shipping it means the build ignored the ruling it was given.

findings.title: Inter as the default font

evidence.snippet: font-family: Inter, sans-serif | first family is Inter

findings.fix: Use the system stack (system-ui, then the platform faces) or the brand face, not Inter.
findings.why: Inter as the first family is the default face of generated UI and flattens every page into the same voice.

findings.title: Text below WCAG AA contrast

evidence.snippet: #6b7280 on #fdf2f8 = 4.43:1, needs 4.5:1 (background #fdf2f8 from body; font-size 14px)

findings.fix: Darken the text token or lighten the surface until the pair clears 4.5:1.
findings.why: Body text under 4.5:1 (or 3:1 for large text) is unreadable for a large share of users.

findings.title: More than one accent hue family

evidence.snippet: indigo (2 uses, e.g. #4f46e5 at line 60); magenta (2 uses, e.g. #ec4899 at line 60); purple (7 uses, e.g. #7c3aed at line 48); red (3 uses, e.g. #ef4444 at line 144)

findings.fix: Keep the accent you use most, and rebuild the second hue as a neutral or a tint of the first.
findings.why: One accent per page is the lock: a second saturated hue family breaks the color hierarchy.

findings.title: Placeholder name in shipped copy

evidence.snippet: SmartFlow in "SmartFlow"

findings.fix: Use a real, contextual name, or a clearly marked placeholder.
findings.why: Jane Doe, Acme and Lorem ipsum mean the copy was never written for a real reader.

findings.title: Filler verb in shipped copy

evidence.snippet: seamless in "Supercharge your team with seamless plan management"

findings.fix: Replace "seamless" with the concrete verb of what the product does.
findings.why: These verbs promise nothing and are the strongest lexical signal of generated copy.
